_README: Batch 20 facts (D-transit) — reconciled 2026-07-24 from deepseek+grok, rulings in disputes-batch20.md. Merge into thailandforamericans/facts.json.
_PANEL_NOTE: The hardened status warning WORKED. Batch 19: deepseek marked 24/40 verified with only 2 official sources. Batch 20: 9/30 verified, all 9 citing airport authorities (airportthai.co.th), airline pages or .go.th sites. Naming the prior failure numerically in the prompt changed behaviour. Keep that pattern.

bangkok_airports._note: Two airports, routinely booked as if they were one place.

which_carriers_use_which.value: Suvarnabhumi (BKK) handles full-service and most international carriers; Don Mueang (DMK) handles primarily low-cost carriers including much of the domestic network
which_carriers_use_which.notes: Both agree; DS cited the Don Mueang airport authority.

distance_km.notes: DS gave 56 km driving / 30 km straight-line; GK gave 38-52. The straight-line figure explains the spread — road distance is what matters and is around 50.

transfer_time_offpeak.notes: Both agree EXACTLY. AOT's own target for the shuttle is about 50 minutes.

transfer_time_peak.value: 90 minutes to 2.5 hours in Bangkok traffic
transfer_time_peak.notes: DS 1.5-2.5h, GK 60-90+. Took the wider band — understating this is the failure mode that costs a flight.

free_shuttle.value: Airports of Thailand runs a free shuttle between the two airports, roughly 05:00 to midnight, taking about 50 minutes in normal traffic and longer in heavy traffic
free_shuttle.notes: Confirmed against the Suvarnabhumi airport authority page.

shuttle_eligibility.value: The shuttle is exclusively for passengers transferring between the two airports. A boarding pass or e-ticket for an onward flight and a passport must be shown; the general public and non-connecting passengers are not eligible
shuttle_eligibility.notes: CRITICAL AND NEITHER MODEL STATED IT PLAINLY. DS said 'requires a same-day flight ticket', GK said only 'for connecting passengers'. The airport authority is explicit that non-connecting passengers cannot use it — so someone overnighting in the city between legs is not eligible.

shuttle_boarding_points.value: At Suvarnabhumi, Level 2 (arrivals) Gate 3; at Don Mueang, the shuttle counter is inside the terminal near exit 6 and must be checked in at before going out to the stop

rail_link.value: No direct rail line connects the two airports. The Airport Rail Link serves Suvarnabhumi and the city, not Don Mueang

minimum_connection.value: No official minimum is published for connecting between the two airports
minimum_connection.notes: RULED. DS explicitly says no official minimum exists and offers industry guidance of 4-5 hours; GK gave '3-4 hours recommended' unsourced. The ABSENCE of an official figure is the honest fact — the guidance numbers are NOT written into prose as if authoritative.

international_to_domestic_steps.value: An arriving international passenger clears immigration, reclaims checked baggage, exits to landside, travels to the other airport, then checks in again from scratch
international_to_domestic_steps.notes: Both agree. The point is that none of it is airside — it is a full re-entry into the system.

main_carriers.value: Thai Airways, Bangkok Airways, Thai AirAsia, Nok Air and Thai Lion Air operate domestic routes

bangkok_to_southern_airports.value: Phuket (HKT), Krabi (KBV), Koh Samui (USM) and Surat Thani (URT) are served from Bangkok

flight_durations.value: Bangkok to Phuket about 1h15; to Koh Samui about 1h; to Chiang Mai about 1h

samui_airport.value: Koh Samui airport is privately owned and operated by Bangkok Airways, which limits which carriers serve it
samui_airport.notes: Both agree. Structurally interesting: the island with an air escape has the most constrained air access.

baggage_allowance_shape.value: Full-service carriers typically include 20-30 kg checked baggage; low-cost carriers commonly sell carry-on-only fares with checked baggage as a paid add-on
baggage_allowance_shape.notes: Both agree; both cited the carrier's own policy page.

change_and_cancel.value: Change and cancellation fees vary by fare class and how close to departure the change is made; the cheapest fares are commonly non-refundable
change_and_cancel.notes: DS cited a carrier page but the shape is generic — kept at verify_recommended rather than promoted.

separately_booked_protection.value: None. A domestic leg booked separately from the international ticket carries no obligation on either airline to rebook or compensate if a delay causes the connection to be missed
separately_booked_protection.notes: Both agree, emphatically. Already established in batch 17's ferry article — this is the same fact reaching the same conclusion from the air side.

through_checked_baggage.value: Baggage is through-checked on a single ticket or between codeshare partners; it is not through-checked across separately booked tickets
through_checked_baggage.notes: Both agree. This is the mechanical reason the previous fact bites — bags must be reclaimed and re-checked.

fare_shape.notes: VOLATILE. Both described hundreds to low thousands of baht one-way. Not frozen.

routes.value: Overnight sleepers run Bangkok to Chiang Mai in the north and Bangkok toward Surat Thani in the south

bangkok_chiang_mai_duration.notes: DS gave specific service times (18:40-07:15 and 20:05-08:45); GK gave 12-14h. Converged on the narrower band DS's schedule detail supports.

bangkok_south_duration.value: About 11 to 13 hours to Surat Thani

arrival_times.value: Overnight services typically arrive early in the morning
arrival_times.notes: Both agree. Decision-relevant: it determines whether the following day starts at the destination or is spent recovering.

class_options.value: First and second class air-conditioned sleepers, with upper and lower berths; fan-cooled options exist on some services

booking_lead_time.value: Popular sleeper berths need booking weeks ahead

bangkok_station.value: Krung Thep Aphiwat Central Terminal is now the main long-distance station for all directions; Hua Lamphong is no longer the primary long-distance terminus
bangkok_station.notes: DS supplied the Hua Lamphong change, which GK did not. HIGH VALUE — most older guides still name Hua Lamphong, so this is a live staleness trap for anyone planning from an outdated source.

airports_and_islands.value: Phuket (HKT) and Koh Samui (USM) serve their own islands directly; Krabi (KBV) serves the Krabi and Ao Nang mainland; Surat Thani (URT) is the mainland gateway for the Gulf islands

islands_without_airports.value: Koh Phangan, Koh Tao, Koh Lanta and Koh Chang have no airport — all are reached by boat
islands_without_airports.notes: Both agree. Consistent with batch 17's ferry article and batch 19's evacuation article, which reached the same list from different directions.

airport_to_pier.value: Reaching the boat-only islands means an onward road transfer from the airport to the relevant pier, then a crossing
airport_to_pier.notes: Both agree. The multi-leg structure is the point.

seasonal_variation.value: Domestic schedules to the southern airports thin out outside high season

evening_service.notes: UNSOURCED. Both described it vaguely and neither could confirm last-departure times. NOT written into prose — this is precisely the fact that would determine whether a same-day connection works, and neither model could source it.

_open_questions._note: Carried from both panel members plus verification.
items: Last departure times from the southern airports — decision-relevant and unsourced by both
Whether any airport or airline publishes an official minimum connection time between BKK and DMK (DS says none exists)
Current shuttle frequency — sources range from hourly to every 12-30 minutes
Whether the shuttle accepts a next-day onward ticket or same-day only — sources differ
